Florina Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Florina, Greece

Demolished. A Sephardi community existed in Florina from the 17th-18th centuries; settlement renewed during the Balkan Wars and WWI with arrivals from Bitola, formally organizing as a 100-family community in 1914. A Jewish school opened in 1917, followed by Zionist organization. 1920s antisemitism and forced Sabbath labor drove many to leave, mostly for Bitola, reducing the community to 293 (of 10,585 total) by 1929, recovering to about 400 by 1940. During WWII, many joined Greek forces against Italian invasion; in early 1943, some joined partisans while 60-70 fled to surrounding hills and villages. On April 30, 1943, 372 Jews were arrested and deported via Salonika to Birkenau; 64 survivors returned postwar, though only 7 remained by 1959. This cemetery's founding is unknown, presumed 20th century.
